memory.title: Prompt translation validator rejects preserved tokens in some languages due to ASCII-only regex (misses tokens with invisible Unicode marks)
memory.root_cause: translation-token-guard.util.ts:18-20 — The placeholder/audio-tag extractors use ASCII-only character classes and don’t strip or tolerate zero-width Unicode formatting/directionality marks inside tokens; tokens like {name} or [laughs] that carry invisible marks are not recognized, causing false mismatches.
memory.fix_summary: Regex extractors for placeholders and audio tags were ASCII-only and didn’t tolerate zero‑width Unicode directionality marks (e.g., LRM/RLM) inside tokens, causing false mismatches. I updated the regexes to allow these marks around/within token names and strip them during extraction, so visually preserved tokens are accepted without changing other behavior.
memory.verdict_reason: Wrong cause: the rejected translations wrap tokens in zero-width spaces (U+200B), e.g. {​name​}; fullwidth brackets are not involved.

finding.hypothesis: Some target-language outputs (notably RTL locales) include invisible Unicode directionality/formatting marks inside preserved tokens, e.g. {‎name‎} or [l‎aughs]. The token guard’s regexes only accept ASCII letters/digits/underscore for placeholders and a–z/digits/[_-] for audio tags, and they do not ignore zero‑width Unicode marks. As a result, visually preserved tokens fail to match, the validator reports them as missing/added, and the translation is rejected. Those languages then fall back to English at runtime.

finding.hypothesis: The helpline routes mount a PageviewTracker that uses the React Router useLocation hook. If PageviewTracker renders anywhere not wrapped by a Router, React throws "useLocation() may be used only in the context of a <Router>" and the root ErrorBoundary shows the app-level crash message. A refactor likely caused PageviewTracker to render before BrowserRouter is established (or during the initial render cycle before Router context is ready), so every page immediately errors after load.

finding.title: Prompt translation token guard rejects preserved tokens with zero‑width spaces, causing false token-mismatch and English fallback
evidence: ally-be/src/prompt/util/translation-token-guard.util.ts:18 — PLACEHOLDER_RE only matches ASCII letters/digits/underscore inside braces: const PLACEHOLDER_RE = /\{\s*([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)\s*\}/g;

finding.hypothesis: Some target-language translations preserve tokens like {name} and [laughs] but wrap them with zero‑width spaces (e.g., U+200B) or insert them inside the token text (e.g., {​name​}, [l​aughs]). The token guard’s extractors only accept ASCII letters/digits/underscore for placeholders and lowercase a–z/digits/[_-] for audio tags, and they do not tolerate zero‑width Unicode marks inside the token. As a result, the preserved tokens are not recognized, validateTranslationTokens reports them as missing/added, the translation is marked FAILED, and runtime falls back to English for those languages.

finding.hypothesis: The Preview tab constructs the `history` payload for each new test message from the entire `turns` array without limiting its length. The backend enforces a maximum of 20 elements for the `history` field; once the conversation exceeds that, subsequent test calls are rejected with 'history must contain no more than 20 elements', even though the on-screen thread still renders. Resetting the thread (New thread) avoids the error because it clears `turns`.
